method: Parse every MW <L> record and its <ls> citations; reduce each citation to its base abbreviation; expand through the vendored MWS tooltip table; fold the IAST expansion to a canonical_text node label. A source label is canonical only when its expansion fold-matches a committed node (or variant); otherwise the raw label is reported under `unresolved` with its MWS expansion.

L.expansion: Lexicographers, esp. such as Amarasiṃha, Halāyudha, Hemacandra, &c.

MW.expansion: On Monier-Williams' authority (many from pandit notes/commentaries; some from Śabdakalpadruma / SKD; some from his own books — NOT the 1872 first edition)

Gal.expansion: Demetrius Galanos's Lexiko: sanskritikes, anglikes, hellenikes

RTL.expansion: Religious Thought and Life in India, also called 'Brāhmanism and Hindūism,' by Sir M. Monier-Williams

IW.expansion: Indian Wisdom, by Sir M. Monier-Williams

MWB.expansion: Monier-Williams' Buddhism in its connexion with Brāhmaṇism & Hindūism: and in its contrast with Christianity

Smṛtit.expansion: Smṛtitattva; the numbers xxix & xxx mark the additional texts Graha-yajña and Tīrtha-yātrā

assumptions: One canonical source label can own many MW <L> records; records are deduplicated per label and keep the first citing source line.
An <ls> base form is resolved only through the MWS abbreviation table and a literal canonical-node match; no model inference or fuzzy title matching.
Editorial markers (L., ib., W., MW., Cat., ...) are reported separately under `nontext`; they are not bibliographic works and receive no passage links.
Unresolved labels keep their MWS expansion for review; they are deliberately not folded into a node by guesswork.
warnings: The index records WHICH MW entry cites a source, not that the quoted passage is the one the label denotes; it is a retrieval aid, not a quotation verification.
Only MW is indexed here. Other dictionaries can be added with the same per-dictionary abbreviation strategy.
